summary: Added the P1 access-control logic layer for the proposed mypintusan (physical access control) app under a new apps/mypintusan package: entities (Holder, Credential, Door, Reader/ReaderProfile, AccessGroup/AccessGroupMember/Schedule/ScheduleWindow/Holiday/Grant, AccessEvent) and services (a pure Decide function implementing the ten ordered gates from docs/MYPINTUSAN_DATA_MODEL.md SS5.1 -- reader health/Secure Channel, lockdown, credential/holder validity, PIN/duress, grant/schedule/holiday, anti-passback, offline-cache policy; Wiegand 26/34-bit decode+encode with parity checking; a Controller that joins the infra/access/osdp bus to the decision path end to end -- decode, resolve, decide, actuate, log, plus lockdown and keypad-then-card PIN pairing; and an injected-clock DoorMachine covering locked/unlocked, door-forced, held-open, and scheduled free-access with first-person-in). 87.3% test coverage, including an end-to-end test against the real OSDP driver and a simulated reader. This is a logic library only: there is no database layer (Store is an interface with only an in-memory test fake -- nothing persists across a restart, no repository/migration/dbsql registration), no apps/mypintusan/apis, no app/ composition root, no config.json, no firstrun/setup wizard, and no frontend, so the app cannot be started. Known gaps stated rather than hidden: Controller.ContactChanged (the myiotsan door-contact seam) is never called by anything; Door.RelayDeviceKey -> myiotsan CommandService.Issue actuation is not implemented (the only shipped Actuator drives a reader's own output); PIN pairing is PIN-then-card only, not card-then-PIN; and Snapshot.AntiPassbackViolation is an input nothing computes (a P3 feature). docs/MYPINTUSAN_DATA_MODEL.md, docs/MYPINTUSAN_HARDWARE_PLAN.md and docs/MYPINTUSAN_OSDP_PLAN.md are updated to reflect this partially-built P1 status.
compatibility: No consuming app exists yet and apps/mypintusan is not wired into app/apphost, any config, or any release pipeline, so this cannot affect any shipping product's behavior, config, API, or runtime flow; nothing to migrate. Scope is deliberately kept at infra rather than a mypintusan app scope: apps/mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, and this repo's version-bump tooling (infra/versioning/bump.go's changeTargets) hard-errors on an unknown scope token rather than silently skipping it -- an app-named scope only becomes valid once that app's manifest entry is created (see README.md's Versioning section, which documents the same rule for myiotsan's P0 scaffolding).
